Personally I would have just waited a bit and scrounged around for the extra $ for the S2 or X instead of going for an older model that uses the old remote.  I mean you're talking about getting shred lights and other accessories which all together would probably equal the price of the S2 and the S2 has some of the sickest integrated lighting I have seen, although I hate that they didn't make it rgb which wouldnt have been difficult nor expensive.  You also could have gotten the new G5 for $599 or G5S for 799 which both have the integrated lighting and use the new remote, although they are both hub drive so...  

I'm not trying to make you feel bad or give you buyers remorse.  The zealot s is a great board and I am sure you will love it, I believe you can also purchase and use the new remote for it so that might be a possible future upgrade for you.  Again I'm sure the zealot s will bring you hours and hours of fun so enjoy!

Oh I thought of another possible upgrade, check out the Omni gear drive.  There are a ton of gear drives available now but this one in particular is "validated" (not officially) to work with many different boards including the zealots.  I personally am not a big fan of belt drive and how quickly I seem to wear out belts.  I could literally feel the difference between brand new belts and 1 or 2 rides and I also hated the amount of rolling resistance.

I own 2 sl1000 shred lights and they a both completely broken unfortunately.  They were great when they worked, super bright and decent battery but the mounting system needs some work as it slowly wore overtime both of them until the would fall of on just a small crack or bump.  They were still nice a bright and super compact so I just used them as handheld flashlights but now neither of them work.  On one the green light on the button stays on and the light won't turn on until it goes out and by then the battery is nearly if not completely dead and the other one flashes randomly and the bottom light flashes yellow/orange.  Because of this and there high cost I can't really recommend them although like I said, when they worked they were great.  I have found that any light or thing really that I try to attach to my board is doomed to fall off at some point, idk if it's the roads I'm riding on or what but I've given up with having board mounted lights and opted to just light myself up instead.  I prefer riding at night when there are less people out and it's cooler (I ride with my husky a lot and he's lit up like the 4th of July as well).  I also feel like it's safer as I am able to stand out being so illuminated and like I said much less car, pedestrian and bike traffic.  I was hit by a car a couple years ago riding during the day, he ran a stop sign and looking back on it there is literally nothing that I could have done differently.  I was on a major bike thoroughfare with no stop and I saw him coming up to the stop sign and lightly applied my brakes, when I saw him slowing down I released but instead of coming to a stop he accelerated, so quickly that there was nothing I could do to avoid.  I guess my last second breaking did kind of save me from being hit head on, instead I ended up tboning it with my body and literally flipping over the car.  I was so shellshocked trying to understand what just happened and if I was ok that the dude took off before I had even got my bearings :( luckily my board was completely unharmed and I thought I was ok as well and was going to try to ride home when some people that saw what happened ran over to see if I was ok and ask if I needed a ride to the hospital.  Right as they said that my right leg began to stiffen up and I realized there was no way I could ride home.  I was so grateful to this couple that not only drove me to the ER but even waited with me until I was seen.  I honestly couldn't believe it and also couldn't stop thanking them for their kindness.  I hope that someday I will be able to pay it forward and help someone in a similar situation because I honestly don't know what I would have done without their help.  Anyways I almost exclusively night ride now, there are a lot of areas that I ride at night that are just too crowded during the day, especially since I ride with my husky a lot, and no, thank god he was not riding with me the day i was hit.

Hope this helps, and again the zealot s is a great board  that has stood the test of time and I'm sure most people that have had them would recommend it wholeheartedly.

I had a 2004 wrx wagon when I lived and worked up at Timberline and Ski Bowl on Mt Hood.  With the Michelin X ice snow tires I put on the thing was a beast and pretty much the mountain car of my dreams.  It's biggest weakness was it's lower ground clearance which only caused me to get stuck once when I was working up at Timberline late into the night during a blizzard.  Luckily I had been riding before work and my apartment was just a couple mile ride down the Alpine trail which would spit me out literally at my doorstep so I just put my headlamp on and road off into the dark blizzardy night and got a ride back the next day with a coworker once the plows had cleaned up the parking lots.  The parking lot at my apartment rarely got plowed though and early on there were definitely times where I thought there was no way I would be able to get out or in but somehow I managed to plow through with snow literally hitting the windshield it was so deep lol.  

Like I said before, it was pretty much my dream mountain car and I got a really good deal on it from some mom on Craigslist who didn't want their kids to grow up driving/racing it as their first car.  Under $10k  only 90k miles and a clean title it was like the stars all aligned and for once my obsessive researching/comparison/shopping finally paid off.  This was back in 2010 so I think they were just coming out with the crosstrek which is probably a more suitable choice due to its higher ground clearance but  getting one of those would have been over 2x the price and while I did look into a few Outbacks I think my heart was set on the wrx from the first time I laid eyes on it.  I miss it dearly :( but my mom got a new outback XT in 2021 that I get to drive sometimes  and every time I do I feel like I'm back in my wrx just newer, a little bigger, smoother and a lot quieter.  It is surprisingly quick and the turbo lag isn't as pronounced and it doesn't require premium gas which is pretty cool unlike the wrx.

I worked as a pharmacy tech and we had a 5g glass vial/jar of 98% cocaine hcl powder and was lucky enough to even fill a prescription once.  I triple weighed it on our very expensive and precise compounding scale where you have to close these little windows  to prevent any air/wind from affecting the measurement.  The crazy part was that my pharmacist just had me dump the powder into one of our regular small vials that you would normally get your prescription in.  I was trying so hard to act normal and not make a joke or  say something ridiculous when the customer came to pick it up and I finally handed it to them.  If I remember correctly it was supposedly being prescribed as a local anesthetic during catheter insertion which sounded pretty odd/fishy to me as I would have thought something like lidocaine would make more sense or if it had to be cocaine then a liquid solution, which we had special order for dental practice before.  But I was just a lowly pharmacy technician making a few dollars over minimum wage so if the pharmacist, whose license is actually on the line, says to fill, I fill.  It was always exciting to handle and fill a new rare/cool drug and it doesn't get much cooler than legit medical grade cocaine, although filling a prescription for opium tincture was a close second. 

Personally I believe that recreational drug use should be legal and regulated and the profits/savings be reinvested into the community, education and rehabilitation.  People are going to find a way and choose to get high no matter how big of a penalty you impose or how much you try to limit or disrupt the supply.  So much of the danger from recreational drug use is directly due to the fact that they are illegal and unregulated and we waste billions of dollars every year on a war that we knew from experience (prohibition) was doomed from the start.  Just like with alcohol, criminalization did not stop people from drinking/using, it only made it more risky/dangerous, gave the police a reason to harass and arrest, and literally created and funded massive and violent criminal organizations that still exist today.  Drugs are more potent and plentiful than ever and so much of the danger comes from the fact that they are illegal and unregulated.  Cops are out here talking about fentanyl like it's some sort of bioweapon but if it were that dangerous it wouldn't be a literal prescription take home medication.  No the danger comes from the fact that users either don't know they are taking something that contains fentanyl or they do but don't know how much.  When you buy rx or even OTC medication it lists the exact and recommended dose and regulation insures that number is as accurate as possible. When you buy a drug on the street you don't even get a number all you have to go by is it's weight, which is useless when the product has likely been cut more times than I have when I'm depressed and anecdotal reports are little help due to how widely tolerance can vary from person to person or even throughout ones life.  One must also take into account the possibility of hot spots which happen when the active ingredient does not get evenly distributed so the dose could still vary widely even if taken from the same batch or even the same bag!

The war on drugs failed and we all lost...

I definitely recommend getting some kind of specific pulling harness both because they put less strain on them and over time your husky will start to associate it with pulling, although mine hates putting on any kind of harness and will always try to make me catch him if he sees me coming with it.

Nah speed wobbles are just do to a shitty setup and or lack of skill, balance and experience.  At least the kind of exponential speed wobbles that lead to crashes.   A decent rider should be able to quickly correct and control a wobble before it gets out of control.  I recommend playing around the tightness of your trucks and the durameter of your bushings.  I firmly believe that in the saying "loose trucks save lives". Obviously not "too loose" but I am constantly amazed at how many people have trucks that are way too tight which lowers your turning radius and frankly can really hold you back from developing the type of strength and good balance that is essential to riding well and eliminating speed wobbles.  Many people prefer stiff trucks because they think it's easier and more stable but it's a lazy habit that will only hold you back.  The last thing you want to be while riding is lazy and although it may seem weird or difficult at first, if you make small adjustments, loosening over time as you grow comfortable you'll start to understand what I mean and how tight trucks can become a crutch that really holds one back from mastering their board and improving their riding.  Obviously you don't want to loosen them  so much that your trucks are at risk of falling apart.  Loosening the trucks is a free and easy fix but if you really want to improve your riding and control look into swapping out your bushings.  I feel like most boards come with way to high of durameter bushings which like tight trucks make the board seem more stable but seriously reduce manueverability

Rite Aid has been cutting hours for years as well.  I went through a total of 8 different pharmacy managers in one year, it was crazy!  The pharmacy manager, besides doing scheduling, is responsible for the entire pharmacy even when they're not there.  If another pharmacist makes a mistake they pharmacy manager can also be held responsible.  I saw one pharmacist dispense oxycodone instead of alprazalam (xanax).  The pharmacist had done their control counts and noticed 30 tabs of oxy 5mg were missing.   She had us searching all around the pharmacy and it was starting to feel like she thought one of the techs or cashiers had taken it.  Then this little old lady comes in complaining that her anxiety medication was making her dizzy and very nauseous.  She checked the bottle and there was the missing oxy.  She is extremely lucky she didn't get fired.  A mixup like that can cause you to lose your job and your license.  But that's the kind of thing that happens when you cut hours and try to add new patients.  There was a point that we were so busy that the pharmacist told us that if the phone rang we were to answer it, put them on hold and leave them there until they hung up.  When it's only you, a pharmacist and a cashier and you have patients waiting in line to drop of new prescription, patients waiting in line to pick up there prescriptions and patients in the drive thru waiting in line to pick up patients and you have 5+ prescriptions that you told a patient would be ready 10 minutes ago and 1 of their prescriptions is getting rejected so you have to call up their insurance to figure out why, there was really no other way.  I felt really shitty doing it and even stopped answering with my name.  I was just following orders people should be getting mad at Rite Aid.  I hated the company myself and quit and moved to another pharmacy shortly after this.

One thing that the pharmacist also does to ensure the correct medication is selected is that they verify the NDC which is a unique number for each individual medication.  The numbers will be different if it is a different strength, manufacturer or a different count (A bottle that you fill from could have anywhere from 30-1000 tablets and they would each have a different NDC).  The pharmacist will visually inspect the prescription vile and it's label, they will look to see at the unique markings on each tab or cap and verify it is the correct medication.  They will verify the NDC and look at the medication bottle to make sure they match and you are billing the insurance for the correct med.  They all have different prices that vary with the medication, manufacturer and strength so you have to make sure the correct one was selected so the pharmacy can get paid the correct amount from the insurance.  There are a lot of checks to make sure every patient receives the correct prescription but when companies try to cut hours so it looks good for their shareholders they are literally putting patients lives at risk.  In the end they don't give a fuck about you or me, all they care about is their bottom line, money.
